title: What If Someone Added One Fish to a Lake? Lake Victoria Did

scenes.text: What if one fish was added to Africa's biggest lake? Hundreds of species disappeared.
In the 1950s, the Nile perch was introduced to Lake Victoria for its meat.
Lake Victoria held hundreds of cichlids, small colorful fish found nowhere else on Earth.
The perch grew huge and ate them. By the 1990s, experts estimated over 200 endemic cichlid species were gone.
Even survivors paid a price. A 2024 genome study found genetic bottlenecks in cichlids from the Mwanza Gulf.
One fish, added for dinner, rewrote a lake. Many of those species exist nowhere else now.
